Thus the specifically referenced feasibility problem has L(f)=-1 for f=C-a^T A b; it is a separating moment problem, not an upper-bounding SOS certificate. The generic statement about a correctly oriented SOS dual is not the error.

witness.explanation: The direction of the moment/SOS separation was reversed.
witness.evidence: If a degree-four functional L is nonnegative on every allowed square and respects the Boolean relations, then any SOS representation f=sum_j p_j^2 modulo those relations implies L(f)=sum_j L(p_j^2)>=0. A feasible separating functional with L(f)<0 therefore excludes that SOS representation; it does not prove f>=0 on Boolean inputs. Such separation also need not supply an actual negative Boolean input.
